Compare fitted models on the same data

Source: R/compare-models.R
compare_models.Rd

Returns a table with one row per model giving its log likelihood, number of parameters, information criteria, classification quality and convergence, together with delta_bic, each model's BIC above the smallest, and bic_weight, the Schwarz weight exp(-delta_bic / 2) normalised over the models compared (Wagenmakers and Farrell 2004). The weight is the approximate posterior probability of each model, assuming one of them is true and all have equal prior probability. No row is marked as best.

Usage

compare_models(..., n_profiles = NULL, n_group_classes = NULL, cutoff = 0.8)

Arguments

...

Either an enumeration grid from enumerate_classes() followed by the candidates to compare (none for all of them, or a selection through n_profiles and n_group_classes); or two or more fits from multilpa(), lpa(), lca(), lta() or get_candidate(); or two or more fits from mixture_regression() (with or without random). Named fits are labelled by their names, unnamed fits by their expression, and candidates by their candidate name. Labels must be distinct.

n_profiles, n_group_classes

With a grid, the class counts of the candidates to compare; NULL (the default) takes every count. Candidates whose fit failed are left out, with a message.

cutoff

For profile and class models, the average posterior probability below which a class is counted in avepp_below and group_avepp_below; a single number in (0, 1], default 0.8. Not used for mixture regressions.

Value

A base data.frame of class latents_comparison, one row per model.

For mixture regressions the columns are model, n_classes, random, n_parameters, log_likelihood, aic, bic, sabic, icl, entropy, smallest_share, delta_bic, bic_weight and converged.

For profile and class models they are model, n_profiles, n_group_classes, structure (the covariance structure, NA without continuous indicators), n_parameters, log_likelihood, every information criterion of enumerate_classes()'s candidates table, profile_entropy, group_entropy, avepp_min, avepp_max, avepp_mean, avepp_below and the same four prefixed group_, smallest_share (the smallest estimated profile share, relative to all observation mass including any noise component), converged, n_best_replicated, and delta_bic and bic_weight, computed on bic_groups (the BIC that counts groups as the independent units; on a single-level model, the ordinary BIC). The values are those of the grid's candidates table.

Raises latents_bad_argument for fits that cannot be compared, for fewer than two models, for duplicate labels, for a group-class family grid (its own table, as.data.frame(grid), compares its candidates), for candidates named together with n_profiles or n_group_classes, and for n_profiles or n_group_classes without a grid; latents_unknown_candidate for a name, counts or selection not in the grid; latents_failed_candidate for a named candidate that could not be fitted; latents_incomparable_models for fits to different data. A cutoff outside (0, 1] fails the argument checks.

Details

Information criteria are comparable only on the same data: every model must be fitted to the same outcome or indicators, persons (or groups) and observations, or the comparison is refused.

Candidates of an enumeration grid are selected by name, as the grid's candidate column shows them (compare_models(grid, "profiles3_groups4", "profiles3_groups5")), or by class counts (compare_models(grid, c(3, 4), c(3, 5)), where a single number means one group class). Alternatively, n_profiles and n_group_classes select candidates: compare_models(grid, n_profiles = 3) compares every candidate with 3 profiles, and compare_models(grid) compares them all. Latent class grids work the same way, with classes in the names, and the n_profiles column counting classes. Fits from multilpa(), lpa(), lca(), lta() or get_candidate() can also be passed directly.

References

Wagenmakers, E.-J., & Farrell, S. (2004). AIC model selection using Akaike weights. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 11, 192–196.

Examples

# Fixed trajectories against growth curves with a random intercept,
# for the first 60 students
few_students <- subset(growth_scores, student <= 60)
trajectories <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, few_students, n_classes = 2,
                                   id = "student", class_level = "group",
                                   seed = 1)
growth <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, few_students, n_classes = 2,
                             id = "student", class_level = "group",
                             random = "intercept", seed = 1)
compare_models(trajectories = trajectories, growth = growth)
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model         Classes  Random     k    LogLik      BIC    ΔBIC  Weight  Entropy
#> ------------  -------  ---------  -  --------  -------  ------  ------  -------
#> trajectories        2  none       7  -1277.94  2584.53  196.11   0.000     0.94
#> growth              2  intercept  9  -1175.79  2388.43    0.00   1.000     0.97

# Candidates of an enumeration grid, by name, by class counts, or selected
grid <- enumerate_classes(subset(course_engagement, student <= 40),
                          c("browse", "lectures"), "student",
                          n_profiles = 2:3, n_group_classes = 1:2,
                          model = "VVI", n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
compare_models(grid, "profiles2_groups2", "profiles3_groups2")
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1458.86  2958.29   0.00   0.999  3233.59     0.67       0.90      0           0.96             0.98
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1454.49  2971.70  13.41   0.001  3409.04     0.67       0.72      1           0.96             0.97
compare_models(grid, c(2, 2), c(3, 2))
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1458.86  2958.29   0.00   0.999  3233.59     0.67       0.90      0           0.96             0.98
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1454.49  2971.70  13.41   0.001  3409.04     0.67       0.72      1           0.96             0.97
compare_models(grid, n_group_classes = 2)
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1458.86  2958.29   0.00   0.999  3233.59     0.67       0.90      0           0.96             0.98
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1454.49  2971.70  13.41   0.001  3409.04     0.67       0.72      1           0.96             0.97
